name: NewColorIris cosmetic implants
lead: NewColorIris is a brand of foldable silicone artificial iris implants that were surgically placed in the anterior chamber of healthy eyes to change eye color for cosmetic reasons. Artificial irises are marketed as an alternative to cosmetic contact lenses, and ophthalmologists have criticized implanting them in healthy eyes because of the risk of vision loss [1].

Published case reports and series describe serious complications after cosmetic implantation, including raised intraocular pressure, glaucoma, corneal decompensation, inflammation and cataract, often requiring removal [2][3][4][5]. A paper on a newer implant, BrightOcular, states that NewColorIris implants have a record of high ocular morbidity and are no longer in use [6].
The evidence consists of case reports and case series rather than controlled trials.
infobox: Described as no longer in use [6]

paras: Cosmetic iris implants are thin colored silicone discs placed in front of the natural iris to give the eye a different color. Patients in published series often had the surgery performed abroad, for example in Panama [3][4].

Prosthetic irises were first developed for medical conditions such as aniridia and trauma; early rigid designs from the 1960s were associated with glaucoma and corneal failure, and later foldable silicone designs emerged in the early 2000s [1]. Cosmetic use in healthy eyes followed, and the implants were reported in medical literature from around 2010 [3][5]. A later design, BrightOcular, added posterior grooves intended to reduce iris contact and improve fluid flow, and has also been associated with serious complications [6][7].

A case series of 14 eyes from a New York eye hospital described serious ocular complications after NewColorIris implantation [2]. Two patients operated in Panama presented with multiple complications and markedly elevated intraocular pressure [3]. A 27-year-old woman presented as an emergency two weeks after bilateral implantation with corneal decompensation, raised pressure and reduced vision; she recovered well after explantation [4]. Reviews of phakic eyes report complications and management after implantation [5][8]. A 2021 study reported complications of cosmetic artificial iris implantation and outcomes after explantation [9]. Surgical techniques for removing the implants have also been described [10].
No controlled trials were found. Human evidence is limited to case reports and case series of patients who developed complications [2][3][4][5][9].

timeline.event: Case reports of serious complications after cosmetic NewColorIris implantation published [3][4].
Case series of 14 eyes with serious complications published [2].
BrightOcular implant complications reported; NewColorIris described as no longer in use [6].
Study of complications and post-explantation outcomes published [9].

card.summary: Silicone iris implants placed in healthy eyes to change color; published case series report glaucoma, corneal damage and vision loss, and the brand is described as no longer in use.
card.aka: NewColorIris, cosmetic artificial iris, BrightOcular (later design)
card.note: Case reports describe serious complications, often needing explantation.

quick.overview:
NewColorIris implants are colored silicone discs surgically placed in healthy eyes to change eye color.

Published case series report serious complications such as raised eye pressure, glaucoma and corneal damage. Ophthalmologists have criticized the use of artificial irises in healthy eyes.
quick.mechanism: A foldable silicone implant sits in front of the natural iris and shows through the cornea in the chosen color.
quick.risks: Reported harms include elevated intraocular pressure, glaucoma, corneal decompensation, inflammation and vision loss, with removal often required. One paper states NewColorIris implants are no longer in use. Evidence is limited to case reports.
